title: credmgrd request lifecycle: six ordered stages before dispatch
caption: Every request passes the same five checks, in this order, before ops::dispatch runs the one step that is operation-specific: peer-uid gate, frame parse, scope resolution (+anomaly), activity touch, auth backoff. Three of those checks can end a request before dispatch ever runs — a non-owning uid closes the connection silently, malformed JSON gets an immediate error reply, and a backoff lockout returns rate_limited — this trace is the path where none of them do. crates/brokerd/src/server.rs (serve_connection, handle_request, peer_is_owner), crates/brokerd/src/scope.rs (resolve_scope), crates/brokerd/src/auth_backoff.rs (remaining_lockout).

messages.label: connect (Unix socket); peer-uid gate: uid == owner (peer_is_owner, once per connection)
(scope, anomaly) — anomaly is recorded, never blocks the request
None -> not locked out, dispatch proceeds
dispatch(state, &scope, now, "entry.reveal", &params) — the one op-specific step
(Ok(value), audit_id) — record_decision already appended the log entry

data_sources.ref: crates/brokerd/src/server.rs (serve_connection: peer::identify_peer + peer_is_owner before the reader is built, then the read_line/parse loop; handle_request: the resolve_scope/touch_activity/auth_backoff/dispatch order; record_anomaly; record_decision)
crates/brokerd/src/scope.rs (resolve_scope: token lookup, workdir match, or global/list-only fallback — never itself an error path)
crates/brokerd/src/ops.rs (dispatch signature and the entry.reveal arm)
crates/brokerd/src/protocol.rs (to_wire; the {id, op, token?, params} / {id, ok, value|error, audit} envelope, per 10_API_AND_MCP.md §1.2)
